problem: Vision-only goal-conditioned navigation policies (GNM/ViNT/NoMaD) trained by imitation degrade in collision avoidance under distribution shift (environment, robot, sensor). They also ignore the robot's physical dimensions and select diffusion samples assuming all are safe.
motivation: Off-road ground robots face variable terrain, sensing degradation and different embodiments. LiDAR gives geometric robustness that RGB lacks, and an explicit learned clearance estimate conditioned on robot size lets the policy reject unsafe samples and escape deadlocks without platform-specific tuning.
key_idea: Fuse RGB, LiDAR (polar-grid PTv3 tokens), goal and robot-size tokens in a transformer that conditions a diffusion trajectory generator, and rank sampled trajectories with a size-conditioned cross-attention clearance head trained on automatically generated LiDAR labels.
insight: LiDAR is the main driver of robustness. Masking images at inference (ViLiNT-Image-Mask) raises SR to 0.72/0.67 in Env. 1/2 vs about 0.33/0.37 for the image-only policies. Adding images on top of LiDAR helps further, most in Env. 3 (0.23 to 0.76). Clearance prediction from image tokens alone (NoMaD-Col) does not help, so the gain comes from 3D geometry plus the clearance-based ranking. Changing the embodiment token changes behavior (a doubled size rejects a narrow corridor).
method: LiDAR tokenizer: PointTransformerV3 per-point features are pooled by GeM in a polar sector-ring grid (K_theta x K_r) with a learned empty-cell embedding, plus angle/radius codes and mean/soft-min range statistics, projected to d-dim tokens.

Multimodal transformer: DUNE ViT image-history tokens, LiDAR tokens, a robot-embodiment token (width, length) and a 2D goal token, with type and temporal embeddings, go through a TF encoder with per-token masking (goal masking, image dropout); attention pooling gives a scene token s.
Diffusion trajectory head: DDPM-style denoiser (T=10 steps) conditioned on s generates J waypoints (x, y, cos, sin); an auxiliary distance-to-goal MSE loss stabilizes training.

Clearance head: a single cross-attention layer where per-waypoint queries (position + robot size) attend to fused LiDAR tokens, followed by an MLP giving per-waypoint clearance normalized by max(w, l). Labels are computed offline from LiDAR point-to-segment distances after ground removal. An asymmetric Huber loss (w_over=5) penalizes over-estimation.

Inference selection: sample N trajectories, take each one's minimum clearance, and among those with clearance >3 pick the one ending closest to the goal. Otherwise take the max-clearance one if >1; if not, regenerate with the goal masked to explore, and unmask the goal once clearance >1.5.

Heterogeneous training: ~98h from RELLIS-3D, TartanDrive2, SCAND, Grand-tour, Huron (no LiDAR, so LiDAR is masked and no clearance loss), plus own Husky and Isaac Sim data; per-dataset waypoint spacing rescaling; frozen image and point-cloud encoders.

setting.backbone: DUNE ViT (frozen) + PointTransformerV3 (frozen) + trained transformer encoder, diffusion head and clearance head
setting.training_data: ~98h35 heterogeneous corpus: RELLIS-3D 35min, TartanDrive 2.0 7h, SCAND 9h, own Husky 30min, own Isaac-Sim 30min (Env.1 only), Huron 75h (RGB + 2D scans), Grand-tour 6h
setting.observation: RGB image history + 3D LiDAR scan (32-beam Ouster) + 2D goal position + robot width/length
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints (position + orientation) tracked by a proportional velocity controller (second waypoint)
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (3 open-field environments) with ROS middleware
setting.privileged: none (goal position in robot frame via LiDAR-inertial odometry)

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 uniformly sampled goals in the environment
numbers.extra: Env.1 simulated data included in training; 10 min timeout, 0.5 m success radius

numbers.backbone: DUNE + PTv3 + transformer + diffusion, images masked at inference

numbers_note: Simulation results are on custom Isaac Sim environments, not a standard benchmark. Values are printed as fractions (0-1) in the table; CR is collision rate. The Env.1 entry is not zero-shot because Env.1 data was in training. The real-world trial count is not given.
results: On three simulated off-road environments ViLiNT gets SR 0.79/0.61/0.76 vs NoMaD-FT 0.33/0.37/0.12, a 166% average SR gain and 62% lower CR. In the real world it reaches 85% SR vs 15% for NoMaD-FT. The non-learned TEB-Elev baseline still reaches higher SR (0.66/0.89/1.00) with zero collisions.
limitations: A classical TEB planner on an elevation map outperforms all learned methods in simulation, and ViLiNT can still fail (e.g. entering empty parking spots, a local-planning limit).

Trajectory selection is decoupled from generation and relies on thresholded goal masking, which can be conservative and cause exploratory detours. Generated trajectories always move forward, so very large robot sizes lead to getting stuck.
Evaluation is on self-made Isaac Sim scenes, with Env.1 data in training, and few baselines. The real-world trial count is unspecified.
